STEP 4.9 stamps that marker on 209 rows every build, so the pipeline erases its own coverage evidence. Measured this run: of 192 events returning centroid_circular, 173 have addresses that INDEPENDENTLY name a real gazetteer municipality - only 19 are genuinely coordinate-only. The spec's circularity concern applies when the city was DERIVED FROM the coordinate; when the address names the city, that is independent evidence and "the address wins" should govern. Coverage is therefore understated for 25 cities: Saint Paul +48, Minneapolis +35, Roseville +20, Shoreview +12 (would move from shortfall to meeting target), Wayzata +7, Edina/Golden Valley/New Brighton +5 each, White Bear Lake +4, Richfield/Brainerd/Bloomington +3 each. Published feed data is UNAFFECTED - this is diagnostic-only. Not changed unilaterally in an unattended run: it is a semantics change to a documented rule and deserves human ratification. Suggested fix: apply circular only on the coord_hit branch.

ROOT CAUSE for a large share of the missing-website backlog: the BiblioCommons fetcher discards each event id at fetch time, so no event URL can be reconstructed afterwards. The gateway returns a real 24-char hex id per event and the canonical URL is https://<code>.bibliocommons.com/events/<id>. Retaining that id at fetch time gives roughly 200 library events a real, non-fabricated website for free. Recovering it after the fact requires re-paginating every system at the gateway hard cap of 10 rows per page (~90 sequential requests), which reliably trips rate limiting - so it must be fixed in the fetcher, not in post-processing.

description: geo0826.py crashed under bycat_shim.py with TypeError: list indices must be integers or slices, not str.
